> [card] [Mirror Access and Permissions](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirror-access-and-permissions.md)
> Understand GitHub-synced access, collaborator sync, and offboarding.
> [card] [Mirrors in CLI](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirrors-in-cli.md)
=== guides/repositories/repository
A repository that is hosted on Entire lives on Entire's Git network with no GitHub origin, so you can push and pull through a region close to where you work: the US, the EU, the UK, India, Singapore, Australia, or Brazil. It has a primary region and can have regional mirrors in other Entire regions.
> There are two kinds of mirrors:
> * **GitHub repository mirrors** are copies of a GitHub repository hosted on Entire. GitHub stays the origin while Entire serves clones and pulls, but forwards pushes to GitHub, so pushes depend on GitHub's speed and availability. See [Mirrors](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirrors.md).
> * **Regional mirrors of a repository hosted on Entire** are copies hosted in regions of your choice within Entire's Git network. They serve clones and pulls locally and forward pushes to the repository's primary region on Entire. Both reads and writes stay within Entire, with no GitHub origin involved.
> This guide covers is about repositories hosted on Entire and their regional mirrors.
* Keep working when GitHub is down. Since your code lives on Entire, your agents can clone, pull, and push without GitHub.
* Work from a single remote. You can push to and pull from the same Entire remote. If you use a regional mirror of your repository that is hosted on Entire, it serves reads locally and forwards pushes to the primary region within Entire.
> At this point, the repository is available in one region, marked `primary`. You can clone, pull, and push without adding a mirror.
> ### 4. Add a Mirror in Another Region (Optional)
> You can add a mirror of your repository to serve clones and pulls from another region within Entire's Git network.
> For this example, if you select `eu-central`, this is how you add a mirror of the repository that is hosted on Entire in another region:
> entire repo mirror add /et/readme/documentation
> A regional mirror of a repository hosted on Entire goes in a region other than its primary region, so only those regions are offered. On a terminal Entire shows them as a multi-select, without one, name the region yourself, because `--cluster` has no default for a repistory:
> entire repo mirror add /et/readme/documentation --cluster aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
> The repository now spans two Entire regions: a primary in `aws-us-east-2` and a regional mirror in `aws-eu-central-1`. Clones and pulls from the regional mirror are served in `aws-eu-central-1`, pushes through it are forwarded to `aws-us-east-2`.
## Convert a GitHub Mirror to a Repository on Entire
Detach an existing GitHub mirror to make Entire your repository's canonical Git source. Detaching preserves the repository's identity, branches, tags, and existing trails and discussions. The GitHub repository stays live but is no longer synced with Entire.
Make sure these requirements are met:
* The [Entire GitHub App](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/github-app-access.md) is installed.
* The repository has exactly one mirror placement, including suspended mirrors. Delete any extra placements before detaching.
* You hold `mirror_source_admin` on the repository group. `manage_settings` alone is insufficient.
* You are a GitHub admin of the source repository. Entire verifies this directly with GitHub using the installation token.
* No mirror removal is pending or in progress for the placement.
* The initial import from GitHub is complete.
> The target [Entire project](https://docs.entire.com/guides/configuration/projects.md) controls who has member access to the native repository after detaching. Access through GitHub and grants on the mirror are removed. Add everyone who still needs access to the target project before detaching.

* Work from a single remote. You can push to and pull from the same Entire remote. If you use a regional mirror of your repository that is hosted on Entire, it serves reads locally and forwards pushes to the primary region within Entire.
> At this point, the repository is available in one region, marked `primary`. You can clone, pull, and push without adding a mirror.
> ### 4. Add a Mirror in Another Region (Optional)
> You can add a mirror of your repository to serve clones and pulls from another region within Entire's Git network.
> For this example, if you select `eu-central`, this is how you add a mirror of the repository that is hosted on Entire in another region:
> entire repo mirror add /et/readme/documentation
> A regional mirror of a repository hosted on Entire goes in a region other than its primary region, so only those regions are offered. On a terminal Entire shows them as a multi-select, without one, name the region yourself, because `--cluster` has no default for a repistory:
> entire repo mirror add /et/readme/documentation --cluster aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
> The repository now spans two Entire regions: a primary in `aws-us-east-2` and a regional mirror in `aws-eu-central-1`. Clones and pulls from the regional mirror are served in `aws-eu-central-1`, pushes through it are forwarded to `aws-us-east-2`.
## Convert a GitHub Mirror to a Repository on Entire
Detach an existing GitHub mirror to make Entire your repository's canonical Git source. Detaching preserves the repository's identity, branches, tags, and existing trails and discussions. The GitHub repository stays live but is no longer synced with Entire.
Make sure these requirements are met:
* The [Entire GitHub App](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/github-app-access.md) is installed.
* The repository has exactly one mirror placement, including suspended mirrors. Delete any extra placements before detaching.
* You hold `mirror_source_admin` on the repository group. `manage_settings` alone is insufficient.
* You are a GitHub admin of the source repository. Entire verifies this directly with GitHub using the installation token.
* No mirror removal is pending or in progress for the placement.
* The initial import from GitHub is complete.
> The target [Entire project](https://docs.entire.com/guides/configuration/projects.md) controls who has member access to the native repository after detaching. Access through GitHub and grants on the mirror are removed. Add everyone who still needs access to the target project before detaching.

content.text:
Short answer: switching fully wouldn't win us anything the prize looks at, and it costs real time mid-hackathon. Mirror now; we can still convert later.

**What the Entire prize judges** (from our challenge notes): how much of Sessions, Graph, Brain and Trails we use, clean history, and measurable token savings. All four work with a mirror:
- Sessions, Graph and Brain are local plus checkpoint refs, so they work either way.
- Trails work on mirrors too. The only difference is that merges go through a linked GitHub PR instead of Entire's own merge button.

**Mirror**
- ✅ Nothing changes for the team: same GitHub repo, PRs, `gh` and agent workflows (including my full-send and PR flow).
- ✅ Teammates get access automatically from GitHub collaborators, with no Entire project invites.
- ✅ Hostinger deploy can keep pulling from GitHub.
- ✅ Reversible: Entire can turn a mirror into a native repo later, keeping its branches, Trails and discussions.
- ➖ Pushes still go through GitHub.
- ➖ Trails merge through GitHub PRs.

**Brand-new Entire repo**
- ✅ Everything in one place, and Trails merge natively on Entire with Gates. It would look a bit more "all-in" in the demo.
- ✅ Faster pushes, and no dependence on GitHub being up.
- ❌ Moves the code off GitHub. Every teammate needs an Entire account and a project invite, and has to change remotes and install `git-remote-entire`.
- ❌ Breaks our `gh` PR workflow mid-hackathon.
- ❌ The Hostinger deploy would need an Entire service account to pull code.
- ❌ It conflicts with the plan's rule that Entire is only worth doing if it takes under 30 minutes and needs no extra work.

If we want the "fully on Entire" story for the demo, we can convert the mirror late on Saturday once the deploy is stable. Entire has a conversion for exactly this, and it keeps the Trails.

So on that welcome page, choose **mirror from GitHub** and tell me "done".

content.content:
With no arguments, launches an interactive wizard: pick repos to mirror, pick one or more regions, then creates every (repo, region) mirror in parallel and prints the clone URLs. --cluster requires a <repo>.

With a <repo>, places it on every cluster named by --cluster — repeat the flag or comma-separate the hosts — in parallel, then waits for each to become usable. Pass --no-wait to return as soon as the placements are registered. Idempotent on (repo, cluster), so naming a cluster the repo is already on reports it rather than failing.

When --cluster is omitted, an interactive terminal offers the available clusters as a multi-select; non-interactive runs default to aws-us-east-2.entire.io.

With an /et/ ref, places replicas of an Entire-native repo and waits for each to be seeded. A native mirror goes in a region other than the repo's own, so only those clusters are offered and --cluster has no default there: non-interactive runs must name one.

Every cluster is attempted: one that fails does not stop the others, and the command exits non-zero naming the ones that did. A GitHub mirror whose initial clone is still running when --timeout passes is reported as still syncing, not as a failure: the clone carries on in the background, and `entire repo view <repo>` shows when it lands.

Repository references name their forge: /gh/<owner>/<repo> for a GitHub mirror, /et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repository.

Usage:
  entire repo mirror add [repo] [flags]

Examples:
  entire repo mirror add
  entire repo mirror add /gh/octocat/hello-world
  entire repo mirror add /gh/octocat/hello-world --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io
  entire repo mirror add /gh/octocat/hello-world --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io,aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
  entire repo mirror add /et/acme/web --cluster aws-eu-central-1.entire.io

Flags:
      --cluster strings        Cluster host(s) to mirror onto; repeat or comma-separate for several (a terminal offers a multi-select when omitted; other runs use aws-us-east-2.entire.io)

      --no-wait[=true|false]   Return once the placement is registered, without waiting for the initial clone
      --timeout duration       How long to wait for mirror request submission, placement, and clone readiness (0 waits indefinitely) (default 30m0s)

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

# Inspect Checkpoints in CLI
Use the Entire CLI when you want to work from a terminal, explain a checkpoint or commit, read transcript output, compare token usage, or export checkpoint data as JSON.
entire checkpoint list
Add `--json` for a machine-readable listing, or `--session ID` to narrow the list to one session.
entire checkpoint search "what changed"
entire checkpoint explain CHECKPOINT_ID
entire checkpoint explain HEAD~3
Add `--full` for the whole parsed transcript, `--raw-transcript` for the JSONL file, or `--short` for the summary alone.
entire checkpoint explain CHECKPOINT_ID --generate
The `--generate` flag requires the configured provider CLI to be installed and authenticated.
## Measure Token Usage
Report token usage and optimization recommendations for a checkpoint:
entire checkpoint tokens CHECKPOINT_ID
The report names the checkpoint, the sessions and agents behind it, the models they used, and the branch, followed by the usage breakdown and the recommendations drawn from it. It reads committed checkpoint metadata through the same resolution path as `entire checkpoint explain`, so an ID prefix or a commit-ish works here as well, and metadata missing locally is fetched from the checkpoint remote.
entire checkpoint tokens CHECKPOINT_ID --compare BASELINE_ID
The comparison reports total tokens, input, cache and context replay, cache write, output, and API calls as a delta against the baseline, and qualifies whether the change counts as an observed reduction or increase.
| `--json` | Output the full report as JSON |
`--json` and `--agent-brief` are mutually exclusive.
> [card] [checkpoint](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference/checkpoint.md)
> See the full checkpoint command reference.

content.content:
> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.entire.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
# runner
> Set up and tune this repository's trail runners.
Manage the trail runner configs in `.entire/runners/`.
> [!NOTE]
>
> File-based repository Runners are separate from project Agents. To configure
> project Agents through the CLI, use [`entire api`](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference/api) as described
> in [Manage Agents from the CLI](https://docs.entire.com/guides/trails/agents.md#manage-agents-from-the-cli).
```bash theme={null}
entire runner SUBCOMMAND
```
`entire runner` is experimental and is hidden from the top-level help. A [runner](https://docs.entire.com/glossary.md#runner) scores and reviews a branch's changes; this command manages the per-repository set: risk, confidence, drift, security, review, and others.
## runner setup
Create and tailor this repository's trail runners.
```bash theme={null}
entire runner setup [RUNNER] [flags]
```
`setup` creates the default runner set in a repository that has none, and tailors the generic templates to this repository using gathered signal: its documentation and structure, merged pull requests and issues, checkpoint churn hotspots, and past trail findings.
In a terminal with no flags, `setup` asks whether you want the generic defaults or defaults tailored to this repository. Otherwise, name the action up front with one of `--yes`, `--defaults-only`, `--print-prompt`, or `--dry-run`. A non-interactive run requires one of them.
`--yes` and `--dry-run` each call your configured summary provider once. With no provider configured and several agents installed, you are asked which to use; `--agent NAME` names one for this run instead and saves nothing.
Pass a runner name, such as `risk` or `trail-risk`, to tune only that runner.
| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--agent NAME` | Text-generation agent to tailor with for this run, such as `codex`. Skips the provider choice and saves nothing. Only applies to runs that tailor: `--yes`, `--dry-run`, or choosing to tailor at the prompt. |
| `--debug-dir DIRECTORY` | Write the assembled prompt as `prompt.txt` and, when a provider runs, its raw response as `response.txt`, to this directory. |
| `--defaults-only` | Create the generic default runners and stop. No tailoring, and no provider call. |
| `--dry-run` | Show the tailoring as a diff and write nothing. |
| `--limit N` | How many recent pull requests, issues, and trails to sample. Defaults to `20`. |
| `--print-prompt` | Create the default runners if missing, then print the tailoring prompt for your own agent to run instead of calling a provider. |
| `--sources SOURCES` | Comma-separated data sources to gather: `repo`, `prs`, `checkpoints`, `trails`, or `all`. Defaults to `all`. |
| `-y, --yes` | Create the default runners if missing, then tailor them to this repository in place. |
```bash theme={null}
# Create the default runners and tailor them to this repository
entire runner setup --yes
# Create the generic defaults and stop
entire runner setup --defaults-only
# Print the tailoring prompt for your own agent
entire runner setup --print-prompt
# Preview the tailoring for the risk runner without writing
entire runner setup risk --dry-run --sources repo
```
> [!WARNING]
>
> `--yes` rewrites files in `.entire/runners/`. Review changes with `git diff -- .entire/runners/` before committing.

> [card] [review](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference/review.md)
>
> Run a multi-agent review against a branch.
> [card] [Glossary](https://docs.entire.com/glossary.md#runner)
>
> See how runners and trails fit together.

## runner setup
Create and tailor this repository's trail runners.
```bash theme={null}
entire runner setup [RUNNER] [flags]
```
`setup` creates the default runner set in a repository that has none, and tailors the generic templates to this repository using gathered signal: its documentation and structure, merged pull requests and issues, checkpoint churn hotspots, and past trail findings.
In a terminal with no flags, `setup` asks whether you want the generic defaults or defaults tailored to this repository. Otherwise, name the action up front with one of `--yes`, `--defaults-only`, `--print-prompt`, or `--dry-run`. A non-interactive run requires one of them.
`--yes` and `--dry-run` each call your configured summary provider once. With no provider configured and several agents installed, you are asked which to use; `--agent NAME` names one for this run instead and saves nothing.
Pass a runner name, such as `risk` or `trail-risk`, to tune only that runner.
| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--agent NAME` | Text-generation agent to tailor with for this run, such as `codex`. Skips the provider choice and saves nothing. Only applies to runs that tailor: `--yes`, `--dry-run`, or choosing to tailor at the prompt. |
| `--debug-dir DIRECTORY` | Write the assembled prompt as `prompt.txt` and, when a provider runs, its raw response as `response.txt`, to this directory. |
| `--defaults-only` | Create the generic default runners and stop. No tailoring, and no provider call. |
| `--dry-run` | Show the tailoring as a diff and write nothing. |
| `--limit N` | How many recent pull requests, issues, and trails to sample. Defaults to `20`. |
| `--print-prompt` | Create the default runners if missing, then print the tailoring prompt for your own agent to run instead of calling a provider. |
| `--sources SOURCES` | Comma-separated data sources to gather: `repo`, `prs`, `checkpoints`, `trails`, or `all`. Defaults to `all`. |
| `-y, --yes` | Create the default runners if missing, then tailor them to this repository in place. |

# Create the default runners and tailor them to this repository
entire runner setup --yes
# Create the generic defaults and stop
entire runner setup --defaults-only

> Run a multi-agent review against a branch and consolidate the results into a final verdict.
Run a multi-agent review against the current branch, or against another branch with `--target`.
```bash theme={null}
entire review [PROFILE] [flags]
```
`entire review` starts reviewer agents in parallel, then uses a judge agent to consolidate their reports into a final verdict.
Reviews are saved as named profiles in Entire settings. On first run, guided setup writes a profile and asks before starting agents.
## Configure a Review Profile
Open the review setup flow:
```bash theme={null}
entire review --configure
```
Use non-interactive flags when you want to create or update a profile from a script:
```bash theme={null}
entire review --configure \
  --set-agents codex,claude-code \
  --set-judge codex \
  --set-output local
```
This creates the default `general` profile unless you choose another profile name in the interactive setup.
## Run a Review
Run a named profile:
```bash theme={null}
entire review general
```
You can also select a profile with `--profile`:
```bash theme={null}
entire review --profile general
```
Scope the review against a specific base branch:
```bash theme={null}
entire review general --base origin/main
```
Add one-off instructions for a single run:
```bash theme={null}
entire review general --prompt "Focus on auth, error handling, and missing tests."
```
Run only one reviewer from the selected profile:
```bash theme={null}
entire review general --agent codex
```
Review a branch other than the one you are on, without switching your checkout. Entire checks it out in a worktree and reviews it there:
```bash theme={null}
entire review general --target feature/token-refresh --cleanup-worktree
```
## Flags
| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--configure` | Set up a review profile. Shows available agents and profiles unless paired with `--set-*` flags. |
| `--set-agents AGENTS` | With `--configure`, set comma-separated reviewer agents for the profile. |
| `--set-judge AGENT[=MODEL]` | With `--configure`, set the consolidating judge. |
| `--set-output MODE` | With `--configure`, set where the verdict is delivered: `local` or `trail`. Defaults to `local`. |
| `--local` | With `--configure`, save to `.entire/settings.local.json` instead of shared `.entire/settings.json`. |
| `--set-task TEXT` | With `--configure`, set the profile's canonical task text. |
| `--set-model AGENT=MODEL` | With `--configure`, set a model for a reviewer agent. Repeatable. |
| `--set-slot AGENT[=MODEL]` | With `--configure`, set one reviewer slot. Repeatable; the same agent or model can appear more than once. |
| **Finding** | A single issue a review [Agent](https://docs.entire.com/guides/trails/agents.md) or [runner](https://docs.entire.com/glossary.md#runner) raises against a branch or [trail](https://docs.entire.com/glossary.md#trail), such as a bug, a regression, or a missing test. When the repository's Findings [gate](https://docs.entire.com/guides/trails/gates.md) is on, open findings at or above its severity threshold block the change from merging until you resolve or dismiss each one. |
| **Line attribution** | Entire's calculation of how many changed lines in a commit came from the agent and how many came from a human. |
| **Metadata** | Structured data Entire records about sessions and checkpoints, including timestamps, agent type, token usage, attribution, and configuration. |
| **Mirror** | A copy of a repository on Entire's Git network in a region of your choice. A GitHub repository mirror keeps GitHub as the upstream while Entire serves Git traffic through one or more regional placements. A regional mirror of a repository hosted on Entire forwards pushes to the repository's primary region. See [Repositories](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/repository.md). |
--
| **Runner** | A config-driven job that runs an AI coding agent in an isolated cloud sandbox against a branch or [trail](https://docs.entire.com/glossary.md#trail). You define runners per repository in `.entire/runners/`. They produce automated review comments, summaries, scores, and findings. Project [Agents](https://docs.entire.com/guides/trails/agents.md), configured on entire.com, are the newer way to review changes and run beside runners. |
| **Search** | Entire's search over every indexed repository you can access, covering both [semantic search](#semantic-search) and [Code Search](#code-search) so one query returns the code and the work behind it. See the [Search overview](https://docs.entire.com/guides/search/overview.md). |
| **Semantic search** | A search over indexed Entire history that matches by phrase, meaning, or agent context rather than by exact words, returning related commits and sessions. Its literal counterpart is [Code Search](#code-search). |
| **Session** | A complete interaction with an AI coding agent from start to finish. Sessions include prompts, responses, code changes, checkpoints, token usage, metadata, and line attribution. |
> Configure saved review profiles for entire review.
Use this page when you want `entire review` to use a saved review setup.
A review profile tells Entire which agents should review a branch, which agent should judge the results, and where the final verdict should go.
For command syntax, see the [`review` command reference](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference/review). For a complete review workflow, see [Review and Recap Agent Work](https://docs.entire.com/learn/review-and-recap-agent-work.md).
## What This Config Affects
Review profile settings control:
* named profiles you can run with `entire review PROFILE`
* the default review profile
* reviewer agents, judge agent, output mode, task text, model choices, and reviewer slots
* whether the review setup is shared with the repository or kept local to your machine
## Configure Review Profiles
> [tab] Shared Project Profile
>
> Use a shared project profile when the team should run the same review setup for this repository.
>
> Create or update a profile with:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> entire review --configure
> ```
>
> You can also configure a profile without the interactive setup:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> entire review --configure \
>   --set-agents codex,claude-code \
>   --set-judge codex \
>   --set-output local
> ```
>
> By default, `entire review --configure` saves the profile to `.entire/settings.json`.
>
> Commit `.entire/settings.json` when the review profile should apply to everyone working in the repository.
> [tab] Local Profile
>
> Use a local profile for personal reviewer choices, private model preferences, or temporary review experiments.

content.text:
The setup is in place, and the $10 is untouched: the billing API still shows `credit_remaining_cents: 1000`. The approach is to use the parts of Entire that are free all the time and save the credit for one demo moment.

**What spends the credit:** only Entire's cloud review Agents and Runners. Sessions, checkpoints, Graph, Brain, search, Trails and `entire review` cost nothing. `entire review` runs on our own Claude Code and posts its verdict to the Trail.

**What I set up (Trail #1 → PR #3, merged as `02e80bf`):**
- **Free reviews on Trails.** `entire review general` is the shared review profile. I tested it on this change: two runs posted 6 findings to Trail #1, and I fixed or dismissed each one with a reply on the Trail.
- **Merge commits only.** Two findings from that review were real. Squash merges were deleting the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers that link commits to agent sessions, so I turned off squash and rebase merging on GitHub. Your first two PRs were squashed, so their trailers are already gone.
- **Codex removed from reviews.** Codex's sandbox can't start on this server, so the review profile is Claude Code only.
- **Team rules in `AGENTS.md`:**
  - one Trail per feature
  - commit while the agent is running
  - run `entire review general` before merging
  - open the PR with `entire trail ci-pr` and `entire trail ready`, then merge with a merge commit
  - never run paid cloud reviews without asking you
- **Plan, section 11 of `PLAN.md`:**
  - **Credit:** keep it for one Sonnet 5.5 Agent run you start by hand on Sunday morning, expected under $1.
  - **Token-savings evidence:** on Sunday, run the same questions with and without Graph and compare them with `entire checkpoint tokens --compare`. We report the measured number as it comes out.
  - I logged this in `DECISIONS.log` and moved Entire from "conditional" to "committed".

**What's left for you and the team:**
1. **Don't turn on any Agents and leave auto top-up off**, apart from that one Sunday run.
2. **Get every teammate installed tonight.** Captured sessions from all four people matter more than anything else here. Each runs the three README commands in their seat (`entire login --device` opens a link they sign in to themselves).
3. **Start fresh agent sessions in your worktrees.** This session started before the hooks were installed, so none of its work is captured.

Merging with merge commits leaves one merge commit per feature on `main`. I think that history is still clean.

# Junction Espoo — shared hackathon workspace

Several people and several AI agents work on this server at the same time. Everything
shared lives in `/srv/junction-espoo`. Each person works in their own git worktree.

## Layout
- `/srv/junction-espoo/<repo>/`: main checkout on `main`. Don't do feature work here.
- `/srv/junction-espoo/<repo>.worktrees/<person>-<task>/`: one worktree per person and task, on branch `<person>/<task>`.

## "handoff read"
When your person says **handoff read**, run `cat ~/HANDOFF.md` on the server (over ssh if you're on
their computer: `ssh -n -o BatchMode=yes junction "cat ~/HANDOFF.md"`) and follow it. It's a note
from the organiser for this seat. If the file doesn't exist, say there's no handoff waiting.

## Rules for agents
1. Before you start, run `je status` and `je log` to see what everyone else is doing and what changed recently.
2. Work only inside your own worktree (the one whose folder starts with your username, see `whoami`). You may **read** other people's worktrees to stay consistent, but never edit, commit, reset, or check out in them.
3. Make your own worktree with `je wt <repo> <task>`.
4. Commit early and often with clear messages. Other agents follow your progress through `je status` / `je log`.
5. Integrate by merging `main` into your branch, or by merging your branch into `main` from the main checkout when the team agrees. Never force-push or rewrite `main`.
6. Dev servers must listen on ports 3000-3099 or 8000-8099. Other local ports are blocked. Run `je ports` to find a free one, and tell the team which port you took.
7. Before you change a shared interface (API shape, DB schema, env vars), check whether another worktree depends on it, and note the change in the repo README or in a `NOTES.md`.

Run `je help` to see all helper commands.

* That a given line was written by a specific agent or person. The tag describes the whole commit, so a line hand-edited inside an `AI` commit still reads as `AI`.
* That the answer survives history rewriting. Both commands follow Git blame, so a rebase, squash, or manual conflict resolution reattributes the line to whichever commit Git now credits.
* Line-level counts. `--long` adds agent, model, author, and session columns, all still commit-level.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `entire blame` and `entire why` are [labs commands](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference/labs.md). They work today, and their output may change.

### Why Doesn't Entire Provide Durable Line-Level AI Attribution?

--
Durable line-level attribution is much harder. In normal team workflows, line-level metadata becomes fragile when:

* Commits are rebased, amended, cherry-picked, or squashed
* Merge conflicts are resolved manually
* Merges happen in hosted Git UIs
* Human edits are mixed into a manual commit before commit time

The core issue is that lines move. A line can shift, split, merge with nearby edits, or be rewritten later. Keeping per-line attribution correct across those changes requires repair logic that runs everywhere history changes.

Entire currently prioritizes a more durable record:

> For checkpoint remote owner rules and push behavior, see [Store Checkpoints in Another Repository](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/store-checkpoints-in-another-repo.md).

> [accordion] A Squash Merge Lost the Checkpoint Link
>
> Some Git hosts can remove commit trailers during squash merges. If the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is removed, Entire cannot link the squashed commit back to its checkpoint metadata.
>
> For GitLab squash merges, configure the squash commit message template under Settings > Repository > Merge requests.
>
> Use a template that includes the squashed commit content, for example:
>
> ```text theme={null}
> %{title} (%{reference})
>
> %{all_commits}
> ```

## Workflow with Entire

- One Trail per feature: from your feature branch run `entire trail create --title "<what and why>" --type feature`. Commits pushed to that branch, and the agent sessions behind them, attach to the Trail.
- Commit agent work with the agent running, so Entire links the commit to its session (`Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer). Don't amend or rebase away those trailers.
- Before merging, run `entire review general`. It reviews locally with Claude Code (no Entire credit; Codex-only users ask a teammate to run it) and posts the verdict to the Trail. Fix or dismiss each finding, then open the PR with `entire trail ci-pr`, undraft it with `entire trail ready`, and squash-merge it while keeping the checkpoint trailers in the squash commit:

  ```bash
  gh pr merge <n> --squash --body "$(git log --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint)' origin/main..HEAD | grep . | sort -u)"
  ```

  A squash without those trailers loses the link between the commit on `main` and its agent sessions.
- Don't run `entire trail rerun-review` or enable project Agents on entire.com: those run paid cloud agents. Ask the repo owner first.
- Never paste keys or `.env` contents into a prompt: transcripts are stored in checkpoints.

# Handoff for ${N}'s AI: join Entire (agent sessions, Graph, Brain)

The team uses Entire (https://docs.entire.com) on the gemini-4-braincells repo. Each commit gets linked to the
agent session that made it, agents look up code with \`entire graph\` instead of grepping, and decisions go into
a shared Brain. The organiser already installed \`entire\` system-wide on the server, along with the graph and brain
plugins for this seat. What's left needs ${N}.

Run every command **on the server**: \`ssh -n -o BatchMode=yes junction "<command>"\` if you are on ${N}'s computer.

## Rules
- ${N} approves the sign-in himself in his own browser. Never approve, submit or click anything on his behalf.
- Never print, copy or upload \`~/.config/entire/tokens.json\`.
- Never paste keys or \`.env\` contents into prompts. Entire stores transcripts.

## Steps
1. Start the sign-in in the background and show the link:
   \`nohup entire login --device > ~/.entire-login.log 2>&1 & sleep 4; cat ~/.entire-login.log\`
   Give ${N} the **Login URL**. He opens it, chooses **Continue with GitHub** with his own GitHub account, and approves.
2. When ${N} says it's done, check: \`entire auth status\` must say **Logged in**.
   If the device code expired, repeat step 1.
3. In each of ${N}'s worktrees (\`je status\` lists them; the folders start with \`${u}-\`):
   - \`git merge origin/main\` (after \`git fetch\`) so the worktree has the Entire files (\`AGENTS.md\`, \`.entire/\`).
   - \`entire brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon && entire brain connect\`
   - \`git status\`: if setup changed tracked files, \`git restore\` them. The organiser manages those files.
   - \`entire doctor\` should report no problems.
4. Mark the handoff done: \`mv ~/HANDOFF.md ~/HANDOFF.done.md\`

## Then tell ${N}, briefly
- From now on, follow the "Workflow with Entire" section in the repo's \`AGENTS.md\`: one Trail per feature, \`entire review general\` before merging, then squash-merge keeping the checkpoint trailers.
- Entire only captures agent sessions that run **on the server inside the worktree**. A session on his own computer that runs commands over ssh is not captured. To have his work count, he can run the agent on the server:

- Don't enable Agents on entire.com and don't run \`entire trail rerun-review\`. Those spend the team's limited Entire credit.
EOF

content.text:
Handoffs are ready. Each teammate just says **"handoff kirill"** (or temuulen / valtteri) to their agent; **"handoff read"** works too.

**What I did for the seats:**
- Installed `entire` system-wide on the server, so every seat and its git hooks can use it without PATH changes.
- Pre-installed the Graph and Brain plugins in each seat, plus the setting for servers with no keyring.
- Wrote `~/HANDOFF.md` for kirill, temuulen and valtteri. Their agent shows them a sign-in link they approve themselves, then sets up Brain in their worktrees and marks the handoff done.
- Updated the shared `AGENTS.md` so "handoff <name>" triggers it.

**One catch to know about:** Entire only captures agent sessions that run **on the server inside a worktree**. Your teammates' agents run on their PCs and send commands over ssh, so their sessions aren't captured unless they run `claude`/`codex` on the server in tmux. The handoff explains how. The same applies to you: this T3 thread runs from `/srv/junction-espoo`, not a worktree, so it isn't captured. Starting T3 threads in a worktree path fixes that.

**Squash merge restored:** I had broken your "always squash merge" rule. Squash merging is back on, and `AGENTS.md` (PR #4, squash-merged) now has a squash command that copies the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers into the squash commit. Entire's docs say that keeps the session links.

**Hostinger online:** yes. Our plan notes say the free VPS (KVM 2, 1 month) and AI Router credits come from the Hostinger booth **or their help channel**, and the help channel is online. Ask there for the hackathon VPS offer. Don't buy one on hostinger.com, because that skips the free offer. It's a hard requirement, so ask tonight. The preliminary submission is also due at **23:55**, about 2 hours from now.
